title: Coefficient comparisons: units, composition and purity
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of the smooth-purity chapter: $k$ is the algebraic closure in the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and $f:X\to Y$ is a smooth separated $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $A\to B$ (and, in clause 2, $B\to C$) be unital maps of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary, uncompleted constant-coefficient pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]; $\Dctf(T,R)$ denotes their bounded objects with intrinsically constructible cohomology [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], meaning that some interval $[a,b]$ contains the cohomology of $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$ for every degree-zero $R_T$-module sheaf $N$.

Use the scalar-extension functors and associators of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the compact-support comparison $b_{A,B}(M):(Rf_{!,A}M)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}(M_B)$ of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], pinned as follows: for a compactification $f=pj$, take the coefficient exchange for $Rp_*$ (the adjunction mate of the coefficient/pullback balancing isomorphism), followed by the canonical coefficient identification for $j_!$, and the counit-characterized comparison $c_{A,B}(K):(f_A^!K)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}f_B^!(K_B)$ of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional]. Write $b=b_{A,B}$, and write $\eta_R,\varepsilon_R$ for the unit and counit of $Rf_{!,R}\dashv f_R^!$. The purity maps $\gamma_{f,R}$ use the diagonal/DNC orientation specified over general finite rings by [det-sp-finite-general-ring].

1. *Units.* For $M\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$,
   $$
   f_B^!\bigl(b(M)\bigr)\circ c_{A,B}(Rf_{!,A}M)\circ (\eta_A(M))_B=\eta_B(M_B).
   $$
2. *Composition.* For $A\to B\to C$ and $K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, the composite
   $(f_A^!K)_C\simeq((f_A^!K)_B)_C\xrightarrow{c_{A,B}(K)_C}(f_B^!K_B)_C
   \xrightarrow{c_{B,C}(K_B)}f_C^!((K_B)_C)\simeq f_C^!K_C$
   equals $c_{A,C}(K)$.
3. *Purity.* For $K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$, in $\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)$,
   $$
   c_{A,B}(K)\circ (\gamma_{f,A}(K))_B=\gamma_{f,B}(K_B),
   $$
   the sources being identified by $(f_A^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq f_B^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$.

proof.text: For clause 1, form the natural compact-support comparison b on the full Dctf subcategories. Its component at M is an isomorphism by det-sp-reduction-direct-image, using the boundedness, intrinsic constructibility and finite Tor amplitude of M. The finite field datum gives characteristic p by the prime-power cardinality of its base field and injectivity of the closure algebra map. Apply injectivity of the inverse B-adjunction Hom equivalence. Precompose both transposes by b_M, which is epic. Naturality of the B-counit at b_M and naturality of b at the A-unit rewrite the composite as T(P_A(eta_A(M))) followed by b_{G_A P_A M}, P_B(c_{P_A M}), the B-counit, and b_M. The specified counit equation hc replaces the middle three arrows with T(epsilon_A(P_A M)). Functoriality of T and the A-triangle identity reduce this to b_M. The transpose of the B-unit is the identity by the B-triangle identity, so its precomposition is also b_M. Cancellation and injectivity prove clause 1. The private counitComparison_unit lemma proves this purely categorical calculation without an additional hypothesis or sorry.

For clause 2, restrict all three support comparisons and both scalar associators to the full Dctf subcategories. The direct-image cocycle is exactly ay(P_A M) followed by b_AC(M) equals T_BC(b_AB(M)) followed by b_BC(T_AB M) and P_C(ax(M)). The AB and BC support components at G_A K and T_AB G_A K are isomorphisms by det-sp-reduction-direct-image; their image and composite are epic. Compare the two proposed exceptional composites using the inverse C-adjunction Hom equivalence and precompose by that epic composite. Naturality of the C-counit at ay_K and naturality of b_BC at c_AB(K) put the BC counit equation into position. Substitute it, combine the T_BC maps, and substitute the AB counit equation. Naturality of ay at the A-counit rewrites the result as ay(P_A G_A K) followed by T_AC(epsilon_A K). The AC counit equation and the displayed direct-image cocycle identify this with the transpose of ax(G_A K) followed by c_AC(K), with the same epic precomposition. Cancellation and injectivity prove clause 2. The private counitComparison_composition lemma supplies the full categorical calculation.

source.place: Proof (2), expanded naturality and inverse-cocycle calculation

proof.text: For purity use the existing generic ordinary-etale finite-ring tensor square: ExceptionalCoefficients.tensorCompatibility states that scalar extension of smoothTensorDualityMap followed by mateMap is tensorDomainMap followed by the B-tensor map. This is the canonical proper/open projection and coefficient-unit counit calculation already proved in the exceptional coefficient comparison module; its private generality applies to every finite ring map, without a quotient or flatness assumption. The private scalarTargetNaturality helper applies naturality of its tensorIso and scalarPullbackIso to a morphism in the second tensor variable.

source.place: Proof (3), Tensor map and Orientation; ordinary-origin realization of the coefficient maps

proof.text: Apply lem-sp-reduction-orientation with exactly the supplied common exponent, deformation geometry, normalized alphaA and alphaB, and generator-normalized e. Its conclusion identifies S_X(alphaA.inv) followed by the coefficient-unit dualizingScalarMap with e.tensorPower(d) followed by alphaB.inv. Expand gamma as one tensor alpha inverse followed by smoothTensorDualityMap. The preceding scalarTargetNaturality moves S_X(alphaA.inv) across the tensor/pullback comparison; tensor functoriality and the orientation equation replace its final factor. The generic tensor square then gives ordinaryGammaCoefficient for every ordinary input. This is a real composition of the tensor and orientation steps; the only new unfinished theorem is the coefficient-unit orientation equation.

source.place: Proof (3), Tensor map and Orientation; ordinary-origin realization of the coefficient maps

proof.text: An intrinsic finite-Tor constructible pro-etale K has a bounded ordinary origin, and the derived comparison counit at K is invertible, by the intrinsicOriginCounit and actualOriginCtf calculations of lem-pur-finite-smooth-level-of-orientation. The scalar-extension lower bound for a finite-Tor ordinary input from the exceptional coefficient module and the derived comparison unit theorem show that the counit at the compared ordinary scalar extension is invertible too. The canonical site/scalar isomorphism followed by scalar extension of the A-comparison counit gives an isomorphism from that compared object to S_Y K; naturality of the B-counit transports invertibility to S_Y K. Thus sourceFromOrigin followed by sourceToOrigin at S_Y K is the identity, by functoriality, inverse cancellation, and cancellation of sourceAtOriginIso.

source.place: Proof (3), Tensor map and Orientation; ordinary-origin realization of the coefficient maps

proof.text: Expand proLambda and cancel sourceFromOrigin followed by sourceToOrigin using the preceding step. Expand proGamma and proCoefficientMap. Naturality of pbcComparisonReduction at the ordinary gamma moves scalar extension across exact site comparison. Apply ordinaryGammaCoefficient at origin_A(K). Finally ordinaryGammaNaturality over B at the specified originReductionMap moves the B-gamma through the remaining origin map. Functoriality of comparison and associativity identify the resulting composites with the exact two sides of reductionCompatibilities_purity. All maps are the existing published constructions. The proof imposes no additional assumption on K or on coefficient flatness.

proof_origin.place: Clauses (1)-(2) retain C9 counit-transpose proofs. Clause (3) by X6: existing generic tensor compatibility, the strictly smaller unit-orientation equation, tensorator naturality, and cancellation of ordinary-origin comparison counits.

split_report.summary: Expanded the unit and coefficient-composition transposes, proved projection compatibility by the existing arbitrary ringed-topos tensor/exchange square and open tensor calculation, and compared diagonal orientations using a single prime-power coefficient origin and the already proved coefficient cocycle. No new nodes. Made the standing scheme domains and meanings of b, c, eta and gamma explicit; retained all three mathematical clauses and arbitrary nonflat finite-ring coefficient maps. Checked exact cited statements, current blueprint and Stacks sources, arbitrary finite-ring etale comparison and projection domains and edge cases. The current imported node has no chapter/unit metadata; this metadata gap is reported without editing maintainer fields. Maintainer-reader fix (2026-10-17): the inline proof of invertibility of the compact-support projection map in Step 5 (finite-ring etale/pro-etale transport of Tag 0F0G) is isolated as the new unsplit node lem-sp-finite-ring-compact-support-projection; Step 7 cites the exponent-independence clause of det-sp-finite-general-ring for computing both purity maps at a common exponent.

The sk-lem-sp-reduction unit constructs the same b and counit-defined c, with its sk-lem-sp-finite-existence and scalar-extension interfaces.

Generic projection/exchange compatibility applied to a ringed coefficient square with identity underlying topoi, required by the tensor paragraph; not a replacement for diagonal/DNC purity.
Open part of the same canonical compactification projection comparison; the coefficient-compatibility balancing calculation is written out.

Its statement defines the general-ring orientation (clause 1, common prime-power origin), the tensor map and gamma_{f,R} with exponent independence (clause 3); clause 3 of the item is about exactly these maps, and no node of sk-lem-sp-reduction defines them.

lean.note: The three named theorems state clauses (1), (2), and (3). Units and composition use the recorded intrinsic Dctf subcategories, adjunctions and counit-characterized coefficient comparison; the latter is expressed equivalently after multiplying by the canonical compact-support comparison. Purity uses precisely the fixed-coefficient presentation and diagonal/DNC-normalized orientations of finiteGeneralRingSmoothPurity, with the published source balancing proLambda and actual counit mate proCoefficientMap. All preservation witnesses and adjunction data are those supplied by the dependency nodes; no coefficient flatness or DVR presentation is imposed.

reviewed_lean.note: Clauses 1-2: unit and cocycle identities in the node's order. GA/adjA/c are arguments because reductionExceptional_isIso gives them existentially; c is fixed by hc (the dependency's counit equation times b, invertible on Dctf); associators are the canonical scalarExtensionFunctor_composition. Clause 3 uses the presentation of finiteGeneralRingSmoothPurity: proGamma; proCoefficientMap, the same c the general-ring node uses; proLambda. Geometry is a Prop class, the orientations are fixed by OrientationNormalized, the CoefficientLineComparison at equal exponents is fixed, the common n>=1 is covered by exponent independence, and HasCompactification is a Prop supplied by the dependency. No flatness, nontriviality, DVR or universe restriction. Edge cases covered: zero rings, d=0, empty schemes, nonflat maps. Only the node's lean field changed; statement verbatim; docstrings with source and proof steps; lines <=100; all proofs sorry. nt_compile --json exit 0 in 6.1 s, no warnings.
